deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to Part II of Riemann's Paris prize essay on heat conduction, the 'Commentatio mathematica' (1861). That part asks when a quadratic form Σ a_{ιι'} dx_ι dx_{ι'} can be transformed into a constant-coefficient form, and introduces the expression later called the Riemann curvature tensor. The page is probably part of the elaborated fair copy prepared for the Gesammelte Werke (1876). The next page carries an editorial note in the editor's voice ('quae auctor scripta reliquit'), which supports this; the hand on this page is not identified here.

(a) Top formula. On the previous page, eq. (9) states that dd Σ a δxδx equals Q/3, where
Q = dd Σ a δxδx − 2 dδ Σ a dxδx + δδ Σ a dxdx.
The previous page also gives 4Δ² = (Σ a dxdx)(Σ a δxδx) − (Σ a dxδx)², where Δ is the area of the infinitesimal triangle spanned by dx and δx.
The curvature measure is then
−(3/8) dd Σ a δxδx / Δ² = −(1/2) Q / (4Δ²).
The denominator on the right is the explicit Gram expression for 4Δ². In modern terms this is the sectional curvature: K(d, δ) = R(d,δ,d,δ)/|d∧δ|², written as a second-variation expression.

(b) Aim. The page announces that it will show this expression agrees with Gauss's measure of curvature of the 2-surface swept out by geodesics from the base point 0. Their initial directions are the linear combinations α dx + β δx, for arbitrary α, β.

(c) Coordinates. Use normal (Riemann) coordinates x_ι = r σ_ι, with σ_ι constant along each geodesic and r its arc length. Normalisation: Σ a σσ = Σ a⁰ σσ = 1, where a⁰ = a(0).
Take two fixed unit directions σ⁰ and σ', and the one-parameter family (12): σ = α σ⁰ + β σ'.
Then α² + 2αβ cos(r₀, r₁) + β² = 1, so the σ_ι depend on a single variable. That variable is chosen as the angle φ between the initial direction of r and that of r₀.

(d) Gauss lemma. Differentiating the normalisation gives Σ a⁰ σ dσ = 0. The property (4) of normal coordinates says Σ_ι a_{ιι'}(x) σ_ι = Σ_ι a⁰_{ιι'} σ_ι, so also Σ a σ dσ = 0.
With dx_ι = r dσ_ι + σ_ι dr:
ds² = dr² Σ aσσ + 2r dr Σ aσdσ + r² Σ a dσdσ = dr² + r² μ dφ²,
where Σ a dσdσ = μ dφ² by definition. The middle term vanishes by the Gauss lemma just stated (my filling of the expansion).

(e) Computing dσ. Start from cos φ = Σ a⁰ σ σ⁰, hence −sin φ dφ = Σ a⁰ σ⁰ dσ.
Because σ stays in the plane spanned by σ⁰ and σ', we can write dσ = a σ⁰ + b σ.
- Pairing with σ⁰ (metric a⁰) gives −sin φ dφ = a + b cos φ.
- Pairing with σ gives 0 = a cos φ + b.
Eliminating a and b (the marginal determinant is Cramer's rule) yields
sin φ dσ_ι = dφ (σ_ι cos φ − σ⁰_ι),
with a = −dφ/sin φ and b = cos φ dφ / sin φ.

(f) Continuation on the next page. From (e), Σ a⁰ dσdσ = dφ². Hence μ = Σ a dxdx / Σ a⁰ dxdx (eq. 13). Setting μ = m²/r² gives Gauss's geodesic polar form ds² = dr² + m² dψ², with k = −m_rr/m. At r = 0 one has μ = 1, μ_r = 0 and k = −(3/2) μ_rr.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The top identity follows from eq. (9) of the previous page: (−3/8)(Q/3)/Δ² = −Q/(8Δ²) = −(1/2)Q/(4Δ²).

Minor imprecision: in the line Σ a σ dσ = Σ a⁰ σ dσ = 0, the index summation is written loosely as Σ_ι in (4). Also, the condition Σ a⁰ σ dσ = 0 is stated as an imposed condition, although it follows automatically from the normalisation Σ a⁰ σσ = 1.
The marginal determinant computation is only a sketch, and its last line is garbled or incomplete. The main-text result sin φ dσ = dφ(σ cos φ − σ⁰) is correct.

results.what: Curvature measure written as a second-variation expression divided by the squared area of the infinitesimal parallelogram, i.e. sectional curvature.
Normal coordinates x = rσ, with the property a(x)σ = a(0)σ, giving ds² = dr² + r² Σ a dσdσ.
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (normal coordinates); Gauss (Gauss lemma for surfaces, 1827)

results.what: Reduction of the n-dimensional curvature to Gauss's curvature of the geodesic 2-surface spanned by two directions, via geodesic polar coordinates ds² = dr² + m² dφ² and k = −(3/2) ∂²μ/∂r² at r = 0.
results.modern_name: Sectional curvature equals Gaussian curvature of the geodesic surface; Taylor expansion of the metric in normal coordinates
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1854; the explicit verification is in the Werke edition of the Commentatio (Weber/Dedekind 1876)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the published material of Riemann's Commentatio mathematica (Part II) as elaborated in the Gesammelte Werke, including the identification with Gauss's curvature. The ideas are well known as Riemann's, and the page appears to be the editorial working-out.

checkable.asserts: Using eq. (9) (dd Σ aδxδx = Q/3), the left side of the top formula equals the right side, with 4Δ² as denominator.

checkable.sympy: a,b,p,dp=symbols('a b p dp'); solve([a+b*cos(p)+sin(p)*dp, a*cos(p)+b],[a,b])
checkable.asserts: The elimination gives a = −dp/sin(p) and b = cos(p)*dp/sin(p), so sin(p)*dσ = dp*(σ cos p − σ⁰).
Euclidean check of sin φ dσ = dφ(σ cos φ − σ⁰); the result should be the zero vector.
Σ a⁰ dσdσ = dφ² (equals 1 per unit dφ), which justifies μ = Σ a dσdσ / Σ a⁰ dσdσ.
If m = r − k r³/6 + ..., then μ = m²/r² satisfies k = −(3/2) μ''(0), as used on the next page.

checkable.sympy: r,dr,s1,s2,ds1,ds2=symbols('r dr s1 s2 ds1 ds2'); A=Matrix([[1,0],[0,1]]); x=Matrix([s1,s2]); dx=r*Matrix([ds1,ds2])+x*dr; expand((dx.T*A*dx)[0]).subs({s1**2:1-s2**2})
checkable.asserts: Expansion ds² = dr² Σσσ + 2r dr Σσdσ + r² Σdσdσ. This reduces to dr² + r² Σ dσdσ when Σσσ = 1 and Σσdσ = 0.

transcription_corrections: Throughout, the image reads dx_ι, δx_ι (coordinate differentials), not ds_ι, δs_ι. The top formula is −(3/8) dd Σ a δx_ι δx_ι' / Δ² = −(1/2)[dd Σ a δxδx + δδ Σ a dxdx − 2dδ Σ a dxδx] / [Σ a dxdx · Σ a δxδx − (Σ a dxδx)²].
'Sint ut supra coordinatae x_ι = r σ_ι', not s_ι = r σ_ι.
The variations of the initial elements are α dx_1 + β δx_1; α dx_2 + β δx_2; ...; α dx_n + β δx_n.
The line 'ds_ι = r dσ_ι + σ_ι dr' should read dx_ι = r dσ_ι + σ_ι dr. Likewise ds² = Σ a dx_ι dx_ι'.
'Iam vero habemus: cos φ = Σ a⁰ σ σ⁰ et −sin φ dφ = Σ a⁰ σ⁰ dσ' is correct. The marginal note is a Cramer's-rule determinant scheme; its last line is unclear.
